note: Initial manufacturer-aware ADAS control catalog, extended in v2 with cross-manufacturer general-pattern entries capped at visually_supported. Small by design: each entry is independently verifiable from the cited source. Certainty describes confidence in the REFERENCE's applicability (confirmed = official document directly verified; provisional = manual mirror or excerpt; definitional = true by control semantics). No manual illustrations are reproduced.

entries.control_description: Vehicle Distance button on the steering wheel; sets the vehicle-to-vehicle follow distance
entries.distinctions: Conventional cruise SET/RES/+/- buttons without a distance function are not ACC evidence. Distance adjustment is the ACC-specific function.

sources.doc: Kia Forte 2021 Features & Functions Guide, Smart Cruise Control (SCC), page 20
sources.section: Smart Cruise Control (SCC): To set the vehicle distance

entries.control_description: Dedicated LKA button on the instrument panel on the lower left-hand side of the driver; cluster lane indicator white (standby) / green (steering)
entries.symbol: lane-assistance button; cluster lane indicator with white/green state semantics
entries.distinctions: NOT Lane Following Assist (LFA): LFA is Kia's separate lane-centering system with steering-wheel buttons. LKA button existence does not establish LFA, ACC, or hands-free capability.

entries.control_description: Driver-assistance button on the end face of the turn-signal lever (E617); opens/configures assistance systems alongside the infotainment Assistance systems menu
entries.symbol: assistance-system button on stalk end face
entries.distinctions: A menu opener: accessing assistance settings does not prove any particular system (lane keeping, centering, ACC) is installed or enabled. Do not infer per-system capability from this control alone.

entries.control_description: Generic ON/SET/RES/+/- cruise buttons with no follow-distance function
entries.distinctions: Evidence of conventional cruise only. Without a distance/follow function these controls say nothing about adaptive capability.

sources.doc: Definitional: a control exposing only set/resume/on-off with no distance function cannot be ACC-specific

entries.certainty_note: True by control semantics, not by manual lookup.

entries.control_description: Lane Following Assist controls on the steering wheel (right side on K5); maintains the vehicle between lane markings
entries.distinctions: Kia LFA is the centering-tier system, distinct from LKA (dash button). Supportive rather than diagnostic here because wheel-button identification alone is weaker than the LKA dash-button case.

entries.control_description: Volkswagen's 'Lane Assist' naming denotes corrective-steering lane keeping (active above ~35 mph), not lane centering or Travel Assist
entries.distinctions: VW Lane Assist is keeping-tier. Travel Assist (centering + ACC combination) and hands-free require their own evidence.

sources.doc: Volkswagen Jetta GLI 2021 Owner's Manual: Lane Assist corrective steering above 35 mph

entries.certainty_note: Naming/interpretation entry (no physical control). Verified via manual excerpts.

entries.control_description: Dedicated lane-keeping control (button or cluster indicator) showing a vehicle-between-lane-lines motif or explicit lane-keeping wording
entries.symbol: vehicle between lane lines; LKA / lane-keeping wording
entries.distinctions: A dedicated lane-keeping control supports LKA only. It never establishes lane departure warning (warn-only), continuous lane centering, highway assistance, or hands-free driving; visually similar motifs are reused across lane-assistance meanings and manufacturer documentation decides.

sources.doc: Road Safety Authority, Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), September 2026 (general driver-education guide; not a manufacturer equipment catalog)

entries.control_description: Dedicated lane-departure-warning control or telltale showing a car-crossing-lane-lines motif or explicit departure wording
entries.symbol: car crossing lane lines; LDW / departure wording
entries.distinctions: A warning-only control never proves corrective steering. LDW does not establish lane keeping assist, lane centering, or any higher tier.

entries.control_description: Assistance-system button, stalk control, or infotainment toggle that opens a menu of driver-assistance settings rather than directly activating one capability
entries.distinctions: The GLI lesson: a stalk-end assistance button opens an assistance-system menu. A menu that can configure several features proves none of them is installed or enabled.

sources.doc: Road Safety Authority, Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), September 2026 (general driver-education guide; not a manufacturer equipment catalog) (symbol/manufacturer-variation disclaimer)

Location-variance example: adas_catalog_v1 entries kia-forte-2019-2024-lka-button (dash-mounted LKA button) and vw-jetta-gli-assist-stalk (stalk-end assistance button opening a menu) show that equivalent controls sit in different places across brands.

entries.certainty_note: True by control semantics: a menu opener cannot identify which menu items are fitted. Never supports any capability claim.

entries.control_description: Dedicated following-distance/gap control (button or rocker) or car-with-distance-bars indicator
entries.distinctions: Only a distance/gap-specific control supports ACC. Plain cruise ON/SET/RES rockers and speedometer-only telltales never establish ACC, and a distance control never establishes Stop & Go, lane centering, or hands-free driving.

entries.certainty_note: RSA general knowledge (rsa_reference.json adaptive_cruise_control): distance-bars motif is the ACC-specific cue. Bare word 'distance' can over-match (e.g. parking-distance displays); the reviewer should confirm the control. Capped at visually_supported.

entries.control_description: Control with explicit lane-centering/following wording (button or cluster indicator)
entries.distinctions: Only explicit centering/following language supports centering; a general lane icon or an LKA/LDW control never does (RSA 6.4). Centering never establishes highway assistance or hands-free driving.
